classes.role: Abstract 3D model base class, a ug renderable. It declares the transform, rotate, translate, scale, copy and draw interface that the software model (fc) implements, and that the HD GL model presumably also implements. It also holds the shared final logic for applying animation frames (AnimBase/AnimFrame tween with label masks) and for tilting a model to the terrain.
classes.obfArtifacts: Essentially none. This class has no invocation counters, no try/catch od.a wrappers, no dummy params and no opaque predicates, so it reads as clean Java. Methods are only renamed to single letters with heavy overloading (a/b/c).
classes.evidence: Declared `abstract class nd extends ug` with one field, `boolean j`. pb sets it before the draw. fc is the only subclass in the SD jar (`final class fc extends nd`, 2672 lines). It has 25 abstract methods. a(int type,int[] labels,int dx,int dy,int dz,boolean) and the masked a(..., int mask, int[]) are the animation transforms. a(int,int,int,int) is the per-bone transform used by a(hf,int). Rotations, verified against fc where U = x, q = y and v = z: a(int) rotates about Z (x/y plane), b(int) about X (y/z plane) and c(int) about Y (yaw). c(), k() and h() rotate 180, 90 and 270 about Y. b(int,int,int) is translate and c(int,int,int) is scale /128. There are three copy variants, a/b/c(boolean,boolean,boolean), that return nd. f() begins animation and returns false when there are no vertex labels. i() is the post-animation update and b() is the height. d(), e(), g(), j() and l() are bounds accessors. The 11-arg a(int x8,long,int,ue) is the draw. Private a(ok base, of frameA, of frameB, int cycle, int delay, boolean[] mask, boolean, boolean, int labelMask, int[]) tweens per transform type ok.E[i]: a 128 default for type 3 (scale), an angle lerp `&2047` with a ±1024 wrap for type 2, a 6-bit hue wrap `&63` for type 7, and `labelMask & ok.w[i] != 65535` selecting the masked transform. Public finals: a(hf,int,hf,int,int,int,boolean) for a single seq; the 14-arg a(hf,...,boolean[] walkmerge,...) for two seqs merged via mask (as in rev-225 Model.applyTransforms); a(hf,...,int mask,int[]); and a(hf,int), which applies only bones with ok.H[] set. a(int[][] heights,x,y,z,sizeX,sizeZ) samples four corners with the bilinear static a(int[][],x,z). It applies b(atan2(dz)*325.95 & 2047) and a(atan2(dx)*325.95 & 2047), then a y translate (terrain conform). The ug method a(int,int,int,int,int) is a final no-op.
classes.notes: Rev-225 Model is concrete. In 530 it is split into an abstract nd plus the SD implementation fc (SoftwareModel), with an HD GL model presumably in runescape_gl.jar. pb's draw casts to fc for merges, so the SD jar has only fc. Animation data classes: hf (frameset holding of[] E), of (AnimFrame: b count, i[] bone index, h/j/p[] xyz, e[] base index, n[] flags, l -> ok), ok (AnimBase: y count, E[] types, v[][] labels, w[] masks, H[] flags). Watch the a(int)=rotateZ / b(int)=rotateX naming when porting.

classes.role: Unlit model geometry, the decoded form of a cache model before lighting. It holds vertex, face and texture-space arrays, decodes the old and extended model formats, and provides merge, copy, recolour/retexture, rotate/scale/translate, ground-conform (hillskew) and normal calculation. It lights itself into a SoftwareModel (fc) through new fc(this, ambient, contrast, lx, ly, lz).
classes.obfArtifacts: None seen. No try/catch od.a wrappers, no client.wb opaque predicates and no division guards in this class. Method names are heavily overloaded (a/b/c/d/e with different descriptors).
classes.evidence: `final class cb extends ug`. The private ctor cb(byte[]) checks `var1[len-1]==-1 && var1[len-2]==-1` and picks b(byte[]) (extended format) or a(byte[]) (old format). Both decoders read through several `new gd(var1)` cursors. Vertex arrays m/l/T (x/y/z), count s. Face arrays C/N/I (a/b/c), count y. Face render type U, priority db, alpha v, texture-coordinate index L, HSL colour p (short[]) and material id H (short[]). Texture-space arrays E/r/F/B/eb/S/A/n/bb/ab/Z/P, count R. fb is the global priority. Vertex labels o and face labels K are grouped into int[][] M and gb by m() (skin groups for animation). e() builds fa[] vertex normals (fields h/m/d/o: sums plus count) and ha[] face normals for type-1 (flat) faces, clamping the cross product to +/-8192 and normalising to 256. Transforms: c(x,y,z) translate; b(sx,sy,sz) scale by n/128; a(int) and c(int) rotate using sin/cos tables `D = dc.g`, `cb = dc.l`; d(int,int,int) rotates on 3 axes; c(), i() and f() rotate by 90/270/180; d() mirrors (negates z and swaps face a/c). b(short,short) recolours and a(short,short) retextures. a(int,int,int[][],int[][],int,int,int,bool,bool) is ground conformance for types 1 to 5, using bilinear heightmap interpolation (>>7, &127). There are ctors cb(cb[],int) (merge), cb(cb,bool,bool,bool,bool) (copy/share), cb(int,int,int) (empty allocation, used by kc) and the private shallow-copy g(). c(5 ints) and b(5 ints) return `new fc(this,...)`. static a(al,int,int) loads model bytes from a Js5 archive; call sites are ja (NPC), jb (loc), fi (identity kit), aj (component) and ai. a(ug,int,int,int,bool) merges shared-vertex normals with a neighbouring model (loc lighting, called from mk/qf). The static scratch arrays G/Y are int[10000], and static l() unloads them. a(...11 params...ue) is an empty Entity draw override.
classes.notes: This matches rt4's RawModel. The 225 client has no separate unlit class because its Model does both jobs, so the 530 name RawModel is kept, as the existing TS already uses it. cb.e() and cb.m() are called at the start of the fc lighting ctor. The Entity overrides (b() returns the cached min Y X after k() bounds calculation; a() returns true) show that cb is itself placeable in the scene as an unlit entity, and a(int,int,int) dispatches to b(t,q,...) to light it on demand.

classes.role: Lit, software-rendered model and the only SD implementation of the abstract Model nd. It owns per-face lit colours, projects vertices (world, simple-perspective and orthographic paths), depth-sorts faces into buckets by priority, near-plane clips, and draws triangles through the Pix3D-like rasterizer dc. It also applies animation transforms (vertex groups, plus alpha and HSL colour groups), ground conformance and mouse picking.
classes.obfArtifacts: No od.a rethrow wrappers, dummy params or opaque predicates. The simple and orthographic draws have an empty catch (RuntimeException) and the world draw has a catch (Exception); both are likely original Jagex code. Three static fc instances (k, V, cb) are reusable scratch models.
classes.evidence: `final class fc extends nd`, the only nd subclass in this jar. The lighting ctor fc(cb,ambient,contrast,lx,ly,lz) calls `var1.e(); var1.m();`, shares cb's vertex, face and label-group arrays (U/q/v = cb.m/l/T, r/N/J = cb.C/N/I, Y/Z = cb.M/gb, G = cb.j vertex flags, u = cb.x), computes `sqrt(lx^2+ly^2+lz^2)`, reads cb.J/cb.hb (fa) and cb.u (ha) normals, and fills per-face lit colours l/M/L. It keeps material ids only where `dc.r.b(0,id)` reports the texture available, and remaps texture-space indices into z/n/H. Transforms: a(int,int[],int,int,int,bool) handles types 0 (origin average over the Y groups), 1 translate, 2 rotate, 3 scale, 5 alpha over the Z face groups, and 7 HSL shift on t, which sets the dirty flag m. The masked/matrix variant a(int,int[],int,int,int,bool,int,int[]) filters vertices with `var7 & G[v]` and takes an optional matrix in var8. a(int,int,int,int) applies the same transform to the whole model. i() calls o() to re-derive the lit colours when m is set and resets the bounds flag K. The draws are a(...11 params...,long,int,ue), the world draw (frustum cull with near 50, far 3500 and the statics oj.j/vf.X/p.l/fl.m, picking gated by oc.m); a(int x7,long), the perspective simple draw with a pick key; and b(int x8), the orthographic draw with a constant scale. a(nd) merges two models via the private ctor fc(fc[],2). a/b/c(bool,bool,bool) copy into the static scratch models V/k/cb so they can be animated. a(int,int,int[][],int[][],int,int,int,bool) does ground conformance for types 1 to 5. Static scratch: 4096-entry projection arrays Jb/Cb/Bb/Fb/rb/Mb, clip flags yb/pb, 1600 depth buckets ib/lb (64 faces each), 32 overflow buckets kb/ub (512 faces each, cap check mb==512), an alternative quicksort path gb/sb (Gb=false), and vb=int[12][4096] priority lists. Near-plane clip at z=50 in e(int) uses the reciprocal table dc.k. Raster calls: dc.a(...) for flat and gouraud triangles, dc.b(...) for textured triangles, dc.o for HSL-to-RGB, dc.f/dc.b for the viewport centre and dc.p for the x-clip edge. classes.role: Glyph font generated at runtime from AWT Helvetica. Each character is rendered to an offscreen Image, captured with PixelGrabber and stored as 9-byte glyph headers plus 8-bit coverage. It draws centred, optionally anti-aliased labels into the Pix2D buffer for the world map.

Drawing clips against td.b/d/e/h and writes into td.g with stride td.c (Pix2D). b(id,...) centres the text, and a(id) measures width while skipping @xxx@ and ~xxx~ tags. Param case0: Q = g1 (interpolation mode), then ab = int[g1][2] markers read as g2 pairs. b(int) (init) defaults the markers to {{0,0},{4096,4096}}, throws "Curve operation requires at least two markers", calls e() to extrapolate the end markers N and O when Q==2, and then f(17142) builds short[] P[257]. classes.role: Procedural texture operator id 37 (factory la.d case 37). classes.role: Instance role: one world-map area definition (rt4 calls it 'Map'). It holds a group/file name, display name, origin, background colour, visible flag, default zoom and a list of ie chunk rectangles, plus a bounding box and a point-in-area test. The obfuscator moved unrelated statics here, so the file is 14.4k lines. Most of that is the CS2 interpreter main loop gh.a(wf,int,int), which Vineflower could not decompile (OOM). gh also holds a cubic-Bezier curve draw and the component x/y alignment routine.
classes.obfArtifacts: Every method is wrapped in try/catch RuntimeException -> od.a(e, "gh.X(...)") rethrow. There is an opaque predicate client.wb (var==0 guards, do/while duplication). Dummy/guard params: d(17882) where !=17882 sets A=35; a(x,z,boolean) where true returns false; the Bezier's var6 must be 3 or L=null; a(aj,byte) where byte>=-63 sets A=52. Per-method invocation counters (D++, V++, K++, O++, E++). Obfuscated shift amounts (e.g. >>1768790380 means >>12, >>-199921906 means >>14). ~a > ~b comparisons. Strings are decoded via vb.a("...",byte). The CS2 method failed to decompile (Vineflower OOM), so only bytecode comments remain and javap all530.javap must be used for it.
classes.evidence: Extends ei (Linkable2/DualNode: t/z prev/next, long v key). Ctor gh(id T, id S, int Q, int R, int J, boolean Z, int H) stores fields, maps H==255 to 0 and sets U = new gk(). Its only call site is the factory hl.a(gd,byte): new gh(buf.l() groupName, buf.l() displayName, buf.c() originX, buf.c() originZ, buf.h() 24-bit colour, buf.f()==1 visible, buf.f() zoom). hl.a then reads a count with buf.f(), appends new ie(c,c,c,c) chunk rects to U, and calls gh.c(0). mc.a fills the static list ba.d from every file of the hl.l group in the he.y archive. c(int) recomputes the bounds: I/W start at 12800 and take the min of ie.B/ie.D, F/ab take the max of ie.y/ie.q. a(x,z,dummy) tests I<=z<=F and W<=x<=ab, then calls ie.a(x,z,16777215) for each chunk. nb.a returns the first area in ba.d with Z set that contains a point. rk.h (also returned by ki.e) is the current area. lg uses rk.h.T (archive name), rk.h.I/F for the scroll origin, and rk.h.H in {37,50,75,100} as zoom. jh.k is another static gh. Statics: gh.a(wf,int,int) is the CS2 executor. Its bytecode references tg.B (int stack) 737x, g.p (string stack) 152x, ad.a/al.B/ai.i (components) and ok.s (Calendar). Callers: gd runs aj.Lb hooks through a new wf (G=args, C=component) with maxOps 2000000; li.java uses 200000. gh.a(10 ints) is a cubic Bezier: 3x coefficients, t stepping 128..4096 in 12-bit fixed point, each segment drawn with ea.a (Pix2D line). It degenerates to one ea.a line when the control points coincide, and si.a calls it. gh.a(aj,byte,w,h) resolves the component's ib/Mb (x/y) from xMode ub / yMode m, using Bc/Ec as base offset and C/H as size. The 6 modes are 0 absolute, 1 centre, 2 right/bottom, 3 proportional >>14, 4 proportional plus centre, and default far edge minus proportional. When uc.c is set, it then clamps the result into the parent. Callers: hf (recursive layout) and ik.
classes.notes: Ownership is mixed. The class identity (world-map area data) plus the CS2 interpreter bulk, about 14k of 14.4k lines, are codex's. Per PORTING.md, statics are assigned individually in membermap.json. The static Bezier curve draw gh.a(int x10) is a Pix2D/raster2d helper that claude should port alongside ea/si. The component alignment routine gh.a(aj,byte,int,int) is interface logic (codex). InterfaceView.ts position() already mirrors its 6 modes but lacks the uc.c clamp. Companion ie is the world-map chunk rectangle (rt4 MapChunk); its fields B/y are one axis range and D/q the other. ie also holds relocated CS2 statics such as H = int[5][5000], the script arrays. The rt4 community name for gh is 'Map'. 'WorldMapArea' avoids clashing with the JS Map built-in. Unrelated static fields also live here because the obfuscator relocated them: C (aj, set by client), M/N (vc/vc[]), L (int[2] resized by d, passed into qc.a by kk), X (e), Y (component id used by bd/kl), B ({1,2,4,8}, used by nc for wall orientation flags), and strings G (empty default for aj string fields) and P. Comments in InterfaceSession.ts and Preferences.ts also mention gh as the CS2 handler.

classes.role: A PcmStream that plays a RawSound (ji) with fixed-point resampling rate, volume, pan, looping and volume/pan ramps. It mixes into the int[] output buffer through many specialised inner-loop kernels.
classes.obfArtifacts: Mostly clean: no od.a wrappers and no dummy params (the sound package appears to have escaped most obfuscation). Methods are synchronized and the kernels take the stream (jc var8) as a trailing param to write back position I.
classes.evidence: extends jj (PcmStream). Constructors copy ji.s/ji.v/ji.u into w (loop start), y (loop end) and x (loop flag); B=rate, C=volume, z=pan (8192 = centre), I=position<<8. Static factories: a(ji,int pct,int vol) = new jc(ji, ji.t*256*pct/(100*mj.e), vol<<6), and a(ji,int,int,int) with pan. Synchronized b(int[],int,int) is the fill and a(int) is the skip. g() recomputes per-channel gains via b(C,z) and a(C,z); the a(int,int) pan law uses sqrt(z*1.2207031E-4F), i.e. 1/8192. About ten private static kernels (byte[] samples, int[] out, ...) handle mono/stereo, forward/backward and ramped mixing, e.g. `var1[var3++] += var0[var2++] * var4` 4x-unrolled with var4 <<= 2. c() returns a 255-capped level, d() returns 0 when silent, e() reports end of stream, D = loop count.
classes.notes: PcmOutput.ts replaces this with WebAudio buffers and cites jc.a's gain shift (<<6 then >>2 in the mono loop). A 1:1 port would need the kernels for exact mixing.

classes.role: Ogg Vorbis codebook. It decodes the codebook header from the Vorbis bit reader, builds the Huffman decode tree from codeword lengths, and unpacks VQ lookup tables (types 1 and 2) for scalar and vector decoding.
classes.obfArtifacts: None (clean class). Only the helpers it calls take dummy args (ei.a(..,(byte)113), kl.a((byte)-22,..)).
classes.evidence: Constructor reads ni.a(24) sync, d=dimensions ni.a(16), c=entries ni.a(24), then ordered or sparse length lists (ni.a(5)+1, kl.a ilog). b() builds a canonical Huffman tree into f (int[8], doubled when full, leaves as ~entry) using the int[33] next-code trick. c() decodes a scalar by walking f with ni.b() bits. Lookup type ni.a(4): min/delta come from ni.c(ni.a(32)) (float32 unpack), value bits ni.a(4)+1, and sequence_p is a bool. Type 1 uses static a(entries,dim) (lookup1Values via Math.pow and ei.a int-pow) and fills float[c][d] a. a() returns a[c()] as the VQ vector. Built in ni.java: y[i]=new dh() (static dh[] y).

Constructor reads ni.a(16) == 1 (floor type 1, else throw), partitions ni.a(5), partition class list h (4 bits each), per class: c = dims ni.a(3)+1, j = subclass bits ni.a(2), b = masterbook ni.a(8), k = subclass books ni.a(8)-1; then multiplier i = ni.a(2)+1, rangebits ni.a(4), X list l[] (l[0] = 0, l[1] = 1 << rangebits). a(): nonzero flag ni.b(), Y values from ni.a(ilog(range-1)) (via kl.a(-22,...)) and codebooks ni.y[book].c(). a(float[],n): low/high neighbour search (static a/b(int[],int)), render_point prediction, step2 flags e[], quicksort a(lo,hi) by X, line rendering a(x0,y0,x1,y1,float[],n) multiplying by f[]. Created in ni.java:211 (I[i] = new lb()), with ni the Vorbis stream/bit reader holding codebooks dh[] y.

classes.role: Vorbis setup-header mapping entry: submap count, channel mux, and the per-submap floor and residue indices. Parsed by the static Vorbis decoder ni.

classes.evidence: The ctor reads entirely from the ni bit reader: ni.a(16) mapping type. d = ni.b()!=0 ? ni.a(4)+1 : 1 (submaps). Optional coupling ni.a(8). ni.a(2) reserved. If d>1, b = ni.a(4) (mux). Then for each submap: ni.a(8) time config, a[i] = ni.a(8) floor, c[i] = ni.a(8) residue. ni.java:222-225 does `X = new fh[a(6)+1]` after the codebooks (dh), floors (lb) and residues (i), and before the modes (G/Q).
classes.notes: Part of the Jagex Vorbis decoder (ni = VorbisSample/decoder, dh = codebook, lb = floor, i = residue). Not yet ported.

classes.role: Vorbis residue header and decoder (residue types 0/1/2): partition classification and cascade books, decoding residue vectors into a float[] using the shared Vorbis codebooks.
classes.obfArtifacts: None. This class is clean: no exception wrappers, dummy params or counters, consistent with the unobfuscated Vorbis package.
classes.evidence: Constructor reads via the ni bit reader: d=ni.a(16) (residue type), a=begin ni.a(24), e=end ni.a(24), g=partition size ni.a(24)+1, b=classifications ni.a(6)+1, c=classbook ni.a(8). Then per classification it reads a 3-bit low cascade plus an optional 5-bit high cascade (ni.b() flag), and f[b*8] book numbers (ni.a(8) or -1). a(float[],int,boolean) zeroes the output, then over 8 passes decodes classification words with ni.y[c].c() split by modulo b, then adds the VQ vectors ni.y[book].a(). The vectors are interleaved when type==0, otherwise sequential. Instantiated only by ni.java:218 (s[i] = new i()), where ni is the Vorbis decoder with codebooks ni.y (dh[]).
classes.notes: Part of the Vorbis stack (ni = VorbisSound/decoder, dh = VorbisCodebook). src/audio has only synth (SoundEffect/Tone/Envelope/Filter); there is no Vorbis yet.

classes.role: Ogg Vorbis audio decoder. It reads the shared Vorbis setup header (codebooks, floors, residues, mappings, modes, MDCT twiddle tables) once from JS5 group 0 and decodes a packetised Vorbis file into an 8-bit signed PCM sound (ji). It also exposes the static bit reader used by the codebook, floor and residue classes.
classes.obfArtifacts: Effectively none. No od.a try/catch wrappers, no dummy guard params and no opaque predicates in its methods, apart from the usual obfuscated call-site dummies such as gd.h((byte)126), gd.f((byte)-44) and al.a(-809612665,...) on the Buffer and Js5 APIs it calls.
classes.evidence: extends jf (Node, so it can be cached). It has a static bit reader over byte[] S with position E and bit offset L: b() reads 1 bit, a(n) reads n bits. dh (codebook) calls ni.a(24), ni.a(16) and ni.c(ni.a(32)). c(int) is Vorbis float32_unpack (mantissa & 0x1FFFFF, exponent (v & 0x7FE00000)>>21, bias 788). Static b(byte[]) parses the setup header: blocksizes P = 1<<a(4) and C = 1<<a(4); for both blocksizes it builds cos/sin MDCT twiddles and bit-reverse tables (kl.a ilog, bi.a reverse); then reads a(8)+1 codebooks into dh[] y, time-domain transforms a(6)+1 x a(16) skipped, lb[] I floors, i[] s residues, fh[] X mappings, and mode tables G (blockflag) / Q (mapping). Instance a(byte[]) reads the header: sample rate x, sample count R, loop start w, loop end A (negative means ~A plus loop flag t), then the packet count and 255-continued packet lengths into byte[][] M. b(packet) does mode, window, floor, residue, inverse MDCT and overlap. a(int[] budget) decodes incrementally and converts floats to bytes via (int)(128 + f*128) - 128, returning new ji(x, bytes, w, A, t). Static a(al,int,int) loads it from a Js5 archive (setup group 0 via a(al) sets J=true), and ll.java:269 (sound loader cache) is its only caller. client.java:1590 calls ni.a() to null the statics on shutdown.
classes.notes: Community names: VorbisSample or VorbisSound (RuneLite: VorbisSample). The helpers dh, lb, i and fh are presumably VorbisCodebook, VorbisFloor, VorbisResidue and VorbisMapping, and ji is the RawSound/PcmSound output (extends kd). There is no Vorbis/MIDI code in src/audio yet (it only has the JagFX-style Tone/Envelope/Filter).

Dummy guard params (var1==67, var0==1, var0==10, var0!=1 -> e=28). client.wb opaque predicate with duplicated irreducible loops. ~x compares. Obfuscated shift amounts (>>>2048219009 == >>>1, >>-1748833343 == >>1).
classes.evidence: static int[] f = new int[256] is filled in <clinit> with the reflected CRC32 polynomial (x>>>1 ^ -306674912 == 0xEDB88320). ik.a(int,byte[],int,int) does crc = crc>>>8 ^ a.f[(b^crc)&0xFF] and returns ~crc. Already ported as src/io/Crc32.ts (comments cite a.f and a.<clinit>). a.a(boolean): when ng.B==2 (ve.f is the ng MIDI player) it loads track qf.m = ee.a(...), builds al.z = new ll(ab.U,g.o) and calls ve.f.a(al.z, 9, 22050, rk.a, qf.m), so music starts at 22050 Hz. Called from client.java:975. a.a(byte): fe.W++, qk.v.k(2,184) (be.k writes isaac-encrypted opcode 184), then for each qd in va.Z with q==0 it calls ok.a(qd,true,15361) (unlink, ra.a/rj.a, ad.a getComponent, ed.a), then if var0==10 clears ca.g via ed.a. This is closeModal, called from bd.java:307, client.java:263 and gh (CS2). a.a(int,byte,int,int,int,int): Bresenham line writing we.z[y][x]=colour, using lk.a for horizontal and al.a for vertical spans. we.z is the procedural-texture raster set by qj.a from gj (a bf TextureOp with a u[] shape list). Called from ea.F (clipped line) and vi's cubic bezier stepper (vi.a, degenerate case plus 32 segments). a.a(int,int[],int,int,int[]): recursive quicksort of keys with a parallel value array, called from fc.java:549 (fc extends nd, software Model) under the Gb flag to sort faces.

The music start goes to the sound/MIDI player (shared). closeModal a.a(byte) goes to interfaces/protocol (codex). The line drawer goes to the procedural texture shape ops (claude). classes.role: Static array helpers: overlap-safe arraycopy for Object[], int[], long[], short[] and byte[], plus int[] clear and fill. Loops are unrolled by 8 (by 4 for long[]).
classes.obfArtifacts: none (no dummy params, no try/catch wrappers)
classes.evidence: No fields. Overloads a(T[] src,int srcPos,T[] dst,int dstPos,int len) for Object/int/long/short/byte: when src==dst and dst lies inside (srcPos, srcPos+len), it copies backwards (memmove behaviour); src==dst with equal positions returns early. a(int[],int off,int len) zero-fills; a(int[],int off,int len,int value) fills (e.g. dk.java:17 cc.a(var3,0,hf.I,cf.h[var1])). Called from id (11 sites), sa (8, BufferedFile), vk (7) and single sites in vg, ug, ri, ok, hh, gi, fj, dk, dg, bd, al.
classes.notes: io/ArrayCopy.ts copyBytes is a 1:1 port of the byte[] overload, keeping the unrolled loop. The other overloads map to TypedArray.prototype.copyWithin/set/fill; only the exact overlap semantics matter.

classes.role: RuntimeException subclass used by the obfuscator's error-reporting wrappers to carry the original Throwable and an accumulated method-signature trace string. uc.a formats it into the error report. Like other obfuscated classes it also hosts unrelated statics: the region terrain loading loop, a chunk-rotation helper, the LOC_MERGE enqueue, the CS2 string stack, and title-screen group-id lookup.
classes.obfArtifacts: The class itself is part of the obfuscator's catch/rethrow error-trace mechanism (od.a -> new g, uc.a formats it). Its own methods have dummy params (var0 >= 53, var8 == 6, var0 != 4, 63/((var0-87)/39)), the opaque predicate client.wb, meaningless shift constants (>>233295656 and >>1450489704, both effectively >>8), and static call counters. The constructor and the unload method have bare catch/rethrow.
classes.evidence: Extends RuntimeException with Throwable a (cause) and String q (trace). Constructor g(Throwable,String). Only od.a(Throwable,String) (od.java:194) creates it: it wraps a non-g throwable in new g(t,s), or appends ' '+s to an existing g's q. Every catch block in the jar throws od.a(e,"cls.M(args)"). uc.a(byte,Throwable) is the reader: instanceof g, then g.q + ' | ', then g.a.printStackTrace(PrintWriter), which builds the error report string. Statics: g.a(byte,bool) walks mk.G (per-region land bytes) with rb.i region ids (>>8 *64 - hk.e, &0xFF *64 - vj.t). It calls nk.a(...) to decode terrain, or bk.a(...) x4 levels to fill missing regions when ah.k < 800. Called from gj during map build. g.a(int,int,int,int): rotation&3 selects z, x, 7-z or 7-x (used by lk for rotated chunks). g.a(13 ints, var8==6) is called only from qd.java:364 (server packet 202). It builds a jk (t,u,D,z,B,E,q,v,s,C,x,y) and pushes it to nl.Q. sg.a(byte) drains the queue: it resolves B to an NPC (uc.l[B-1]) or a player (te.g/tf.J), finds the scene loc by th.e[shape], removes it via b.a, and sets ob.nb model, ib/y cycles, Wb/k position and bounds. That is LOC_MERGE. g.a(int,al) sets ed.a = al.a(groupIdByName 'titlebg') and da.h = 'logo' (client.java:2107). g.a(int,int): if qg.a(id) loaded interface group id, calls fk.a(-1,..,fk.ab[id]). Called from db/gf with root hd.m and recursively from fk for subinterface qd.v. g.a(0): if ph.d != null, calls fi.b(-1,ph.d) (world-map setmap) and clears it (gj). g.p = new id[1000] is the CS2 string stack (gh pops g.p[--var7]). g.j = new wj(), g.o al, g.l = ')2'. g.k/g.n are statics used in fk and f.
classes.notes: The class itself is error-reporting infrastructure (shared/util). A TS port does not need it if the od.a wrappers are dropped. For the statics: the region-terrain loop g.a(byte,bool) is scene loading (claude), next to scene/MapSquare.ts (nk.a/fi.a). The LOC_MERGE enqueue g.a(13 ints) and its sg.a consumer are game state (codex); ZoneState.ts already parses op 202 as a 'merge' effect. g.p is the CS2 string stack (codex; ScriptStack in script/ScriptRunner.ts). The titlebg/logo lookup is in ClientLoading.ts. g.a(int,int) is interface component handling (codex).

World-map ownership boundary: the definitions and data (gh, ie, kc, nb) are codex. The rendering (eg, mi, oc, and the world-map statics in ah, mj, og and uh) is claude. gh also hosts the CS2 interpreter. Please confirm this split.

namingNotes:
I checked all 289 entries with a script (C:\Users\jorda\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\9c24769301cc7750\7e1824b4-0347-487d-a365-01a4331e7de0\scratchpad\check.js against the decomp class list). Every obf appears exactly once. Names and paths are unique, including case-insensitively. Only the allowed packages are used, no reserved path is reused, and every owner is claude or codex (184 codex, 105 claude). 125 entries changed. No files were modified. PORTING.md was only read: the user said Codex is coordinating there. Its live tree was used to align names.

Naming rules applied:
- **225 names first, where the role matches:**
  - Datastructs: Linkable, Linkable2, LinkList, LinkList2, LruCache, HashTable, JString.
  - io: Packet, Isaac, BZip2, ClientStream.
  - client: KeyCodes, MouseTracking, Client, GameShell.
  - sound: Envelope, Filter, Tone, JagFX.
  - Every config type: IfType, VarBitType (capital B), and the rest.
  - Every dash3d scene and entity name, including Sprite for ec (repo file src/dash3d/Sprite.ts).
- **Otherwise community names (rt4/RuneLite).**
- **Family conventions:**
  - A '2' suffix marks a Linkable2-based variant: Linkable2, LinkList2, HashTable2, ByteArrayNode2.
  - Value holders are named *Node. A node that wraps an entity takes the entity's name plus Node: ClientObjNode, ClientProjNode, MapSpotAnimNode.
  - Software implementations are Software*: SoftwareModel, SoftwareFont, SoftwareSprite, SoftwareAlphaSprite, SoftwareIndexedSprite. Their HD counterparts can then be Gl*.
  - An abstract base whose plain name is taken gets an Abstract prefix: AbstractSound, AbstractSprite, AbstractIndexedSprite.
  - Textures: TextureProvider (kg) implements TextureLoader (pc) and caches Texture (qi), which wraps ProceduralTexture (jd). Then TextureOp*, TextureShape*, and Colour/MonochromeImageCache(+Entry).
  - British 'Colour' throughout, as the 225 code uses (Colour, getColour).
  - JS5 classes pair Net and Disk: Js5NetQueue/Js5NetRequest and Js5DiskQueue/Js5DiskRequest/Js5DiskCache.
  - Static cached lookups use the *List style: ParamTypeList, FloTypeList, MapSceneTypeList, ScriptList, AnimFramesetList.
  - Static-only buckets are named after their dominant routine (SceneDraw, GameReset). Mixed or field-only buckets are <Theme>Statics. No name contains obfuscated letters.

Packages:
- **dash3d:** scene graph, entities (225 keeps ClientEntity/ClientNpc/CollisionMap/LocChange there), models, animation, Pix3D, textures.
- **graphics:** Pix2D, sprites, fonts, the PixMap family, GameCanvas.
- **js5:** every JS5 class, including the request classes and the byte copiers.
- **io:** packets, ISAAC, compression, streams, files, protocol, world list.
- **client:** the shell, input, timers and game-state buckets.
- **ui:** interface logic and the world map.
- **util:** Signlink and error/platform helpers.
- **wordfilter:** Huffman.
- **gl:** this SD jar has no GL classes.

Logical names deliberately left free for member-map targets: World (dash3d/World.ts, for the scattered scene statics), MiniMenu, MiniMenuAction, TitleFlames, ByteArrayPool, Preferences, InterfaceList.

Where Codex's in-tree names were consistent, I adopted them: Js5DiskCache, Js5DiskQueue, Js5DiskRequest, EnumStringEntry, and the *List style.
